question.problem:
$\,$ $P(x):$ $x\in N$ $\,$ $Q(x):$ $x\in Z$

Consider the predicates $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ above. Which of the following expresses the conditional predicate $P(x)⇒Q(x)?$

I. If $x\in Z,$ then $x\in N$

II. $x\in Z$ if $x\in N$

III. $x\in N$ implies $x\in Z$

IV. $x\in N$ only if $x\in Z$
question.worked_solution:
Let's recall the following grammatical constructions for the implication $P⇒Q:$

- If $P,$ then $Q$

- $P$ only if $Q$

- $Q$ if $P$

- $P$ implies $Q$

With that in mind, let's examine the given options.

- Option I reads

$$
\text{if}\,{{x\in Z}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)},\,\text{then}\,{{x\in N}_{⏟}}_{P(x)}
$$

which corresponds to $Q(x)⇒P(x).$ $\,\times $

- Option II reads

$$
{{x\in Z}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)}\,\text{if}\,{{x\in N}_{⏟}}_{P(x)}
$$

which corresponds to $P(x)⇒Q(x).$ $\,✓$

- Option III reads

$$
{{x\in N}_{⏟}}_{P(x)}\,\text{implies}\,{{x\in Z}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)}
$$

which corresponds to $P(x)⇒Q(x).$ $\,✓$

- Option IV reads

$$
{{x\in N}_{⏟}}_{P(x)}\,\text{only if}\,{{x\in Z}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)}
$$

which corresponds to $P(x)⇒Q(x).$ $\,✓$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II, III and IV only."
